Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

WildObsR (development version)

New

  • effort_matrix() and detection_matrix() build detection histories with sampling effort for occupancy and abundance models (#140, #110). Effort is calculated from the deployments alone, as fractional camera-days per local calendar day, so it never depends on where animals were detected, and every camera in a site counts. Occasions are non-overlapping runs of w days, aligned per site or to the calendar for multi-season models; effort can be split by a deployment column (for example featureType) for use as an observation covariate, and long-term deployments rebuilt with recombine_deployment_groups() exclude the gaps between their pieces. Detection histories are NA only where no camera ran, and a detection on a day its camera was not running stops with an error. On single-camera stations both agree with camtrapR::detectionHistory(). They work on any Camtrap DP package.
  • effort_matrix() uses UTC days, with a message, when the deployments span several time zones, given as several time_zone values or found from the cameras’ coordinates. Zone names that keep the same clock over the survey count as one. To split effort by two columns, combine them into one first (see ?effort_matrix).
  • model_matrix_input() adds total_effort, each site’s camera-days over the modelled occasions, as a site covariate (and to det.covs for single-season spOccupancy and spAbundance output). ?model_matrix_input explains when to use it rather than the per-occasion effort, and how it differs from the resample’s cellEffort.
  • model_matrix_input() formats those detection histories, with site and observation covariates matched to sites by name, for unmarked (occu(), pcount(), occuComm(), and colext() with seasons), spOccupancy (PGOcc(), msPGOcc(), tMsPGOcc() and their spatial versions), spAbundance (NMix(), msNMix()), or as plain arrays for JAGS, NIMBLE or Stan. Camera-days of effort, and the share of effort under each level of an effort_matrix() split_by column, are added as observation covariates.
  • example_datapackages() reads two open projects shipped with the package (ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001, systematic and unbaited cameras in the Queensland Wet Tropics; NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010, wombat burrows and controls in New South Wales over four surveys in 2021-22), in the same shape wildobs_dp_download() returns. Examples, tests and tutorials now run offline on real data. The copies hold animal observations only, no media and no email addresses, and are rebuilt from the public API by dev/make_example_data.R. The examples of extract_metadata(), extract_tags(), recombine_deployment_groups(), locationName_buffer_CAPAD() and locationName_verification_CAPAD() now run on them.
  • cite_datapackages() turns a list of downloaded data packages into a reference list: formatted text, BibTeX (utils::bibentry) or a table. It uses each package’s own bibliographicCitation word for word (WildObs citations end with the project’s RAiD) and adds the project’s WildObs data package version, which rises whenever WildObs corrects that project’s data, so a reader can tell which version was analysed. Packages without a citation, such as other Camtrap DP datasets, get one built from their contributors, year, title and link. covariates = TRUE also cites, once each, the products behind the covariates table (forest integrity, human footprint, climate and so on), each named by the covariates it is behind (e.g. FLII), and accessed adds the download date.
  • recombine_deployment_groups() rebuilds long-term deployments from the 100-day pieces the curation pipeline cuts them into, for multi-season occupancy, trend indices and other long-term analyses (#109). A data package goes in and a data package comes out:
    • Pieces of one camera (locationID × multiSeason_deploymentGroup × the _CamN suffix) are joined into one deployment named <locationID>_ms<N>[_CamN][_partN].
    • A gap longer than max_gap_days (default 30) between pieces starts a new _partN run, since one station can sit idle much longer than the 30 days that separate multi-season groups. Pieces of one camera that overlap in time stop the function with an error naming them.
    • Deployments and covariates are collapsed, and deploymentID is remapped in observations and media. Differing values are merged by a rule per column type: duration-weighted means for numbers, the value covering the most time for factors and date-times, and deploymentTags keeps each key once, preferring real values over placeholders such as unspecified. Missing values stay NA.
    • A new deployment_crosswalk resource keeps every original piece with its pieceStart and pieceEnd. Calculate sampling effort from it, since the recombined start-to-end span includes gaps of up to max_gap_days.
    • dp$temporal holds one block per multiSeason_deploymentGroup; the package-level start, end and timeZone are unchanged. dp$data is refreshed to match.
    • Obscured threatened-species records (obscured_for_<category>_species) are kept unchanged, with a message saying how many.

Documentation

  • A pkgdown website, https://wildobs.github.io/WildObsR/, with twelve tutorials in three groups. Get the data: Get started, Discover what exists, Inside a WildObs data package, For data providers. Use the data: Images for computer vision, Camtrap DP interoperability, Spatial context. Model the data: Detection histories and sampling effort, Fit single-season models (unmarked, spOccupancy, spAbundance and NIMBLE), Fit multi-season models (colonisation and extinction, and trends), and Combine projects to ask one question. Working with Claude introduces the bundled Claude skill.
  • Tutorials that need the WildObs API are knitted ahead of time by vignettes/precompute.R, so the website and R CMD check run without a key.
  • CITATION.cff and an updated citation("WildObsR").

Bug fixes

These change the matrices matrix_generator() returns; regenerate any results built with it.

  • matrix_generator() uses non-overlapping sampling occasions and retains the final day and partial occasion. Detection and observation covariate matrices use the same windows (#140). This changes results previously affected by duplicated boundary days or omitted final days; regenerate downstream effort matrices that mirrored the old windows.
  • matrix_generator() with all_locationNames = FALSE now drops the landscapes where a species was not detected from the site covariates as well as the detections (#105).
  • matrix_generator() counts a sampling unit as sampled until its sampling ends, not until its last record, so a camera that kept running gives zeros rather than NA.
  • matrix_generator() places records on their local day rather than their UTC day, which moved morning records in eastern Australia to the day before.
  • matrix_generator() returns site covariates in the same order as the matrix rows, keeps sampling units with no observations as zeros (with a message), no longer carries a shortened dur from one species to the next, and no longer drops a species whose observation covariates do not vary.
  • matrix_generator()’s input checks now run; they used to pass any input. Observation covariates that are not columns, and sampling units in obs without covariates, stop the function. NA values in site or observation covariates are kept, with a warning, since unmarked drops the affected units or occasions itself. Text date columns are converted to date-times, with a message, and a value that cannot be read stops the function.
  • resample_covariates_and_observations() groups observations by their local day, in the time zone their eventStart is stored in, rather than the UTC day. Records between midnight and 10 am AEST used to be merged into the previous day, which moved some detections into the previous occasion in matrix_generator(). On project 0001, the legacy and new detection histories now agree exactly.
  • matrix_generator() uses UTC days, with a message, when the sampling units span time zones with different clocks; otherwise records fall on their local day, as before.
  • matrix_generator() no longer drops site covariates: one with the same value everywhere is kept (standardised to 0 if numeric), and logical and factor covariates, such as the resample’s mode_baitUse, are kept too.
  • matrix_generator() warns when numberDeploymentsActiveAtDate is used as an observation covariate. It counts only the deployments with a record that day, so it understates effort and depends on detections. Use effort_matrix() for effort.
  • resample_covariates_and_observations() keeps logical and factor columns in both tables (for example baitUse and featureType from frictionless::read_resource()). They used to be dropped silently. A column keeps its class and factor levels when every cell holds one value, and modal columns always do; a column where some cell holds several values is pasted as text (for example "FALSE - TRUE"), with a message naming it.
  • spatial_hexagon_generator() now warns when several projects sample one cell at overlapping times, listing the cells at each scale by their polygon_<scale> value and the projects involved. The check used to group by project as well, so it could never fire. Each project keeps its own cellID, as before.
  • resample_covariates_and_observations() warns, rather than stops, when a sampled cell has no observations, for example after filtering obs to a few species. The cell stays in the resampled covariates as sampled with no detections. Observations in a cell with no covariates still stop with an error.
  • resample_covariates_and_observations() now weights each deployment by its camera-days when averaging covariates (Avg_*) and taking modes (mode_*) within a cell, so a camera that failed after 2 days no longer counts as much as one that ran 90, and a redeployed station no longer counts once per redeployment. Coordinates stay plain means. On typical projects values move by a few percent of the spread between cameras in a cell; regenerate resampled covariates to pick this up, or pass weights = "none" for the previous plain means.
  • resample_covariates_and_observations(obs = NULL) resamples the covariates only, which is all model_matrix_input() needs for site covariates and takes seconds rather than minutes. Its tables are tagged with their scale, and effort_matrix() and detection_matrix() now stop with a message naming the right table when given resampled covariates or observations: effort needs the deployments with their cellIDs, and detections the observations themselves.
  • detection_matrix(by_camera = TRUE) now stops, with an explanation, when the effort matrix was built with split_by. It used to place detections by camera number in a dimension that holds the split levels, misplacing them or failing with “subscript out of bounds”. ?detection_matrix now spells out how abundance counts are combined (the largest count per event, then summed or maximised over events), and ?resample_covariates_and_observations what its individuals = "sum" does and does not count.

Breaking changes

  • WildObsR now requires R 4.1 or later, which the native pipe |> used in the package already needed.
  • wildobs_mongo_query() now returns open and partial projects by default (tabularSharingPreference = c("open", "partial")), so a search shows every project a public key can see, including embargoed ones whose data exist but are not yet released. Partial projects download as metadata only: their data package has no resources, so code that calls frictionless::read_resource() on every downloaded package stops on them. Either ask for open projects only, wildobs_mongo_query(..., tabularSharingPreference = "open"), or skip the metadata-only packages before reading their tables: dp_list <- Filter(function(dp) length(dp$resources) > 0, dp_list).

Fixed

  • resample_covariates_and_observations() no longer stops when a column named in mode_cols_covs or obs_covs is entirely empty (for example habitat in a project that never recorded it). Such columns are left out with a warning naming them.
  • resample_covariates_and_observations() no longer stops when a cell’s cameras recorded no observations, which happens whenever observations are filtered (to animals, or after setting obscured records aside). Those cells are kept in the resampled covariates as effort without detections, and a message names them. Observations in a cell with no camera still stop the function.
  • Date-times downloaded over the API could be shifted by the computer’s offset from UTC (ten hours in Queensland). The API sends dates as MongoDB {"$date": ...} objects, and when an optional date field held both dates and empty values in one response, jsonlite read the dates in local time rather than UTC. Required fields (deploymentStart, eventStart, media timestamp) are never empty and were not affected; classificationTimestamp was, depending on where you were and which projects were downloaded together. WildObsR now reads every API date as UTC before applying the project’s time zone.
  • Ready for frictionless 2.0.0 (#136). From that version frictionless::add_resource() writes Data Package v2 tables, which lack the profile = "tabular-data-resource" that Camtrap DP 1.0.x requires, so as_camtrapdp() exports would have failed the Camtrap DP profile. wildobs_dp_download(), recombine_deployment_groups() and as_camtrapdp() now keep every table in the v1 form with either frictionless version. The full test suite passes against both frictionless 1.3.0 and 2.0.1. WildObsR now requires frictionless 1.3.0 or later, the first version with resource_names() and schema().
  • The wildobs_mongo_query() help no longer says the function filters out projects still under embargo. Embargoed projects are stored as partial until the embargo ends, and the help now says so. Its example uses api_key rather than an undefined db_url.
  • wildobs_dp_download() over the API now downloads any number of projects in one call. Previously each table came back in a single request, and asking for many projects at once failed with HTTP 504 because the response was too large to arrive before the API timed out. Each table is now fetched in pages: 10,000 deployments, 50,000 observations or 5,000 covariate rows at a time. All 23 open projects now download in one call in about three minutes.
  • After the pages are in, the number of rows in each table is checked against the server’s own count, and wildobs_dp_download() stops with an error rather than return part of a table. Obscured threatened-species observations, which share one placeholder observationID, are fetched separately so paging cannot skip them.

WildObsR 0.3.0

The WildObs database now follows the Camtrap DP standard more closely, and earlier versions of WildObsR cannot read the updated metadata: wildobs_dp_download() stops with incorrect number of dimensions. Update WildObsR to download data again.

devtools::install_github("WildObs/WildObsR")

Breaking changes

dp$temporal keeps the database’s shape

Downloaded packages now store temporal exactly as the database does: the package-level start, end and timeZone once at the top, then one {start, end} block per deploymentGroup. Previously timeZone was copied into every group. Code that read dp$temporal[[1]]$timeZone should read dp$temporal$timeZone instead, or use extract_metadata(dp, "temporal"), which handles both shapes.

Spatial functions no longer take a shapefile path

ibra_classification(), locationName_verification_CAPAD() and locationName_buffer_CAPAD() now use the IBRA7 and CAPAD 2022 layers that ship with the package, so they work on any computer. The ibra_file_path and capad_file_path arguments are gone: remove them from your calls. The layers are available directly as the datasets ibra and capad (#11, #122).

locationName_verification_CAPAD() now measures CAPADminDistance in true metres. Previously it measured in web Mercator units, which overstate distances in Australia by roughly 10–40% depending on latitude, so values will be smaller than before and the 1–5 km / 5–10 km / >10 km notes may change category.

wildobs_mongo_query() returns an empty vector when nothing matches

When no project matches, wildobs_mongo_query() now returns character(0) rather than "", still with a warning. length(result) > 0 is now FALSE, and loops over the result no longer run once with a blank ID. Code that tested result == "" should test length(result) == 0 instead. wildobs_dp_download() stops with a clear message when given no IDs, including the old "" (#129).

dp$sources is a list of sources

sources is now an array of source objects, as Camtrap DP specifies, so dp$sources[[1]]$title replaces dp$sources$title. extract_metadata(dp, "sources") returns one row per source.

New

  • as_camtrapdp() converts a WildObs data package to canonical Camtrap DP 1.0.2 (or 1.0.1), so it works with the camtrapdp R package, including camtrapdp::write_dwc() for GBIF. It removes every WildObs addition, read from the official Camtrap DP profiles vendored in the package rather than a fixed list, and returns a report of every change and the result of validating it (#113). Its camtrapdp element is the result already read by camtrapdp::read_camtrapdp(), so it goes straight into camtrapdp functions: camtrapdp::write_dwc(out$camtrapdp, dir).
  • wildobs_media_download() downloads the image files listed in a media table into out_dir/<projectName>/<deploymentID>/<mediaID>.<ext>, and reports what happened to each file. Publicly hosted files (filePublic = TRUE) download for anyone; files on your own computer are copied; private Google Cloud files can be fetched with a gcs_token if you have access. Re-running fetches only what is missing.
  • install_claude_skill() installs wildobsr-data, a Claude skill describing how WildObs data packages are structured and what the data can support, so Claude can help with your analysis. See “Help Claude understand WildObs data” in the README. It describes the data as API users receive it, including how obscured threatened-species records behave and how to set them aside.
  • extract_metadata(dp, "temporal") gains packageStart and packageEnd columns holding the package-level temporal extent (#137).
  • Downloaded packages now include versionControlWildObs, the WildObs version of the package.
  • Covariate fields in downloaded schemas now carry a custom block with the source citation and resolution of the spatial product behind each covariate, and media fields keep their pattern constraints.

Fixed

  • wildobs_dp_download() skips project IDs it cannot find, with one warning naming them, and downloads the rest. It stops only when none are found. Previously an unknown ID failed with “subscript out of bounds” (#129).
  • apply_schema_types() gives empty datetime columns the POSIXct type, and converts partly empty ones. Previously a column with any empty cell was treated as unparseable and left as text, or as logical if wholly empty (#129).
  • apply_schema_types() no longer deletes a datetime column whose schema field has no format: it falls back to ISO 8601, and leaves the column unchanged with a warning if it still cannot parse it (#129).
  • wildobs_dp_download() no longer hides warnings from typing the tables, so a column that fails to convert is reported rather than passed on silently (#129).
  • apply_schema_types() accepts the Frictionless any type and leaves such columns unchanged, so media downloads no longer warn about exifData.
  • wildobs_mongo_query() checks a spatial bounding box before querying and names any missing or non-numeric corner, instead of failing with an internal tibble error (#129).
  • ibra_classification() no longer drops locations that fall just outside every IBRA subregion. They now take the IBRA values of their nearest matched location, as documented (#97).
  • locationName_buffer_CAPAD() generates UTM coordinates when they are missing. Its check matched any column name containing “x” or “y”, including deploymentID, so it always skipped generation and stopped with “No unique UTM zones found”.
  • locationName_verification_CAPAD() no longer leaves its internal ID, lat2 and long2 columns in the output.
  • locationName_buffer_CAPAD() stops with an error naming any deploymentID used more than once. Previously rows sharing an ID were silently merged into one.
  • wildobs_dp_download() reads the updated database structure.
  • wildobs_mongo_query(temporal = ...) no longer errors on the package-level temporal extent, and still matches projects on when each deploymentGroup ran.
  • extract_metadata() still reads data packages saved by earlier versions.
  • wildobs_dp_download(api_key = ..., media = TRUE) no longer fails after the media download with argument is of length zero. Public media tables, which withhold fileName, get an empty fileName column on every route.
  • wildobs_dp_download() over the API retries a request that fails or returns an error, up to three times, instead of failing with subscript out of bounds. A large media download makes hundreds of requests, so one dropped request used to end it. If a request still fails, the error names it and gives the server’s reason; a media download no longer returns partial results silently.
  • wildobs_dp_download() no longer duplicates observations of a taxon listed twice in a project’s taxonomic metadata. It keeps the first listing and warns which taxa were repeated.

Internal

  • The update notice now only appears for a new major or minor release, not for patch releases.

WildObsR 0.2.0

This is a breaking release. Some functions you may have called directly are no longer available, and the bundled API key has been removed. The three changes most likely to affect you are listed first, each with what you need to do.

Breaking changes

The bundled API key is gone — create your own

Earlier versions shipped a shared API key as a dataset called wildobsr_api_key. That dataset has been removed and the key it contained no longer works.

What to do: create a personal API key on the WildObs Dashboard, store it in your .Renviron file, and read it in R with:

api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY")

Keys are tied to you personally rather than to a project. The README has a step-by-step walkthrough under “Getting Database Access”. Treat your key like a password: do not paste it into a script that you share or commit.

Nine helper functions are now internal

These were previously callable with WildObsR::function_name(). They are still in the package and still used by it, but they are no longer part of the public interface, because they are helpers for other functions rather than tools meant to be run on their own:

clean_list_recursive(), convert_df_to_list(), extract_classif(), find_closest_match(), is_empty_spatial(), is_empty_temporal(), long_to_UTM_zone(), reformat_fields(), reformat_schema()

What to do: if a script of yours calls one of these with WildObsR::, it will now fail. Most of them were only ever used inside other WildObsR functions, so in practice you probably do not call them at all. If you genuinely need one, it can still be reached with three colons, as in WildObsR:::convert_df_to_list(), but that is a stopgap rather than a promise: internal functions can change or disappear without notice. Tell us which one you need and we will consider making it public, as we did this release for the two functions listed under New below.

Two of the nine have changed further since: is_empty_spatial() has been removed outright, and find_closest_match() is deprecated. Both are covered below.

MongoDB document helpers removed

mongo_clean_df(), mongo_format_dates() and mongo_prepare_doc() have been removed. All three prepared data for writing into the WildObs database, which is not something this package does — it only reads. They now live in the private repository used to run database updates.

What to do: nothing, unless you were calling them directly, which would only be the case if you help maintain the database itself. Downloading and querying are unaffected.

Deprecated

Both still work exactly as before, and both now print a warning the first time you use them in a session. They will be removed in a future release.

  • check_schema() has been retired from the data intake workflow. Schema validation now happens inside the download itself, so you no longer need to run this as a separate step.
  • find_closest_match() is no longer used by the package. It warns only once per session rather than once per call, because it is often passed to sapply() where a per-call warning would flood your console.

What to do: if either appears in a script, plan to remove the call. Nothing breaks today.

Removed

  • gbif_check() — had no callers anywhere in the package or in our other repositories.
  • is_empty_spatial() — had no callers and no known external usage. is_empty_temporal() is unaffected and still works.

New

Two helpers are now public

Both were already being used from other WildObs projects, so they have been given proper documentation, examples, and unit tests, and are now supported:

  • rename_or_add_column(df, new_name, old_name) renames a column, or adds a new all-NA column if you pass "", NA, or nothing as the old name. Note the argument order: the new name comes before the old name. Some mobilisation markdowns define their own copy of this function with the arguments the other way round. Those local copies still take precedence in your own script, so nothing changes for you until you delete one — at which point check the order at every call site.
  • get_decimal_places(x) counts significant decimal places in a number, ignoring trailing zeros. Used to work out coordinate precision.

WildObsR now tells you when it is out of date

The first time you call wildobs_mongo_query() or wildobs_dp_download() in a session, the package checks whether a newer version has been released and warns you if so. It never stops your work, and it stays completely silent when you are up to date or when GitHub cannot be reached.

Attaching the package with library(WildObsR) also runs one quick check that the WildObs database is reachable. It prints nothing unless something is actually wrong.

The README now explains what major, minor and patch version numbers mean, so you can judge whether a given update is urgent.

Internal

None of these change how the package behaves, but they make it install more reliably:

  • geojsonsf added to Imports. It was already being used but never declared, so anyone who did not happen to have it installed hit an error.
  • tidyselect and httr2 removed from Imports. Neither was used any more.
  • utils added to Imports, for the version check.
  • The Author field in DESCRIPTION was malformed and has been replaced with a proper Authors@R entry including an ORCID.
  • A standard R-CMD-check GitHub Actions workflow now runs on every push and pull request, across macOS, Windows and Linux.
  • R CMD check is now clean: no errors and no warnings, down from three warnings.
  • The test suite grew from 819 to 890 passing tests, including the first tests for rename_or_add_column() and get_decimal_places().
